name: github_backlog_intake_airlock
title: GitHub Backlog Intake Airlock
description: GitHub Backlog Intake Airlock is a six-node RailCall workflow for engineering leads who need to turn a supplied CSV backlog into governed GitHub issues without silently duplicating prior work. parse_csv handles quoted CSV locally, validates the required header, preserves source-row evidence, and accepts optional prior_replay_keys from a previous signed receipt. validate admits only new/ready rows with GitHub-safe title and body lengths while separating failures, review holds, and terminal rows. dedup normalizes title/body pairs, collapses same-batch duplicates, and assigns each candidate a deterministic versioned replay key. replay_guard suppresses keys already recorded by an earlier successful run. create_issue fans out only over eligible rows through github.create_issue; RailCall approval is required before any GitHub write. reconcile fans in the provider results, issue numbers, landed keys, suppressed keys, and the exact next_prior_replay_keys list for the next run. All parsing and replay logic is pure: no files, sockets, credentials, clock, or hidden provider lookup. The sample produces two eligible previews, one same-batch duplicate, one validation failure, one review hold, and one terminal row. A second run using the first receipt's next_prior_replay_keys produces zero GitHub effects. contest:2026Q3
